decisions.rationale: 'breast cancer' in the title names the disease under study as one specific disease entity with no further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Annotate all Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: 'tumor' is retained as a disease term (cancer and tumor are kept) and here modifies the noun phrase 'cell lines', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Modifiers for other concepts; What NOT to Annotate 4: 'cancer' and 'tumor' are retained

decisions.rationale: 'breast and ovarian cancer' is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), so it is one Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2: Annotate contiguous text strings (Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: 'malignant effusions' only names the specimen source (fluid samples) and describes a general finding or complication rather than a named specific or class disease, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4: Do not annotate general terms (e.g., complications, abnormalities)

decisions.rationale: 'breast cancer' in 'many breast cancer biopsies' is a disease name modifying the noun 'biopsies', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'breast cancers' is the head noun referring to a family of multiple diseases, explicitly divided into sporadic and familial forms, so it is a Disease Class mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Disease Class (mentions describing a family of multiple specific diseases)

decisions.rationale: 'sporadic' is an adjective describing the type of cancer, not a disease name, so it is not a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4: Do not annotate general terms; only disease name mentions are annotated

decisions.rationale: 'familial' is an adjective describing the form of cancer, not a disease name, so it is not a disease mention.
